transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in today?

Hi. Well, I'm here because I'm having a major issue at work. I manage construction sites, and lately, every time I have to get near a scaffold, or a roof edge, or an upper platform... my head just tells me I'm about to go over. 

It's getting really bad. Even when I can clearly see the guardrails are in place, and I know for a fact the setup is supposed to be completely safe, I just can't shake it. My brain just convinces me I'm going to fall.
When the thought that you might fall comes up, do you feel driven to perform any repetitive action or mental ritual to prevent it or reduce your anxiety?

No, nothing like that. I don't... I don't have any rituals or repeat things to myself. I mostly just freeze up, honestly. Or I just have to back away from the edge as fast as I can to get the panic to stop. But no, I don't do any specific repetitive actions.

final_diagnosis.reason: Marked, immediate fear and avoidance of heights despite recognizing the objective safety of the situation, with freezing and withdrawal that interfere with occupational functioning, are most consistent with specific phobia, situational type (acrophobia). No compulsive rituals were reported, making obsessive-compulsive disorder less likely; panic disorder is less likely because panic symptoms are limited to height-related situations and recurrent unexpected attacks were not established.

additional_requirements: Fear is focused on heights and is disproportionate to the objective danger
Avoidance or escape behavior is present
